skill.name: schema-markup
skill.description: Design, validate, and optimize schema.org structured data for eligibility, correctness, and measurable SEO impact. Use when the user wants to add, fix, audit, or scale schema markup (JSON-LD) for rich results. This skill evaluates whether schema should be implemented, what types are valid, and how to deploy safely according to Google guidelines.

content.value_statement: Schema markup is easy to overuse and can violate rich result rules. This skill evaluates eligibility and designs accurate JSON-LD for safer SEO implementation.
actual_capabilities: Scores pages with a 0-100 Schema Eligibility and Impact Index.
Recommends supported schema types such as Organization, Product, FAQPage, Event, and BreadcrumbList.
Drafts JSON-LD implementation guidance with placement instructions.
Checks visible content alignment, required properties, and spam policy risk.
Provides validation steps for Rich Results Test, Schema.org Validator, and Search Console.
limitations: Does not guarantee Google rich results or ranking changes.
Requires accurate visible page content and business data from the user.
Does not run external validators directly.
Cannot validate claims that are not present in provided page content.

use_cases.title: Audit Launch Pages
use_cases.description: Review page content, current schema, and Google eligibility before a release.

use_cases.title: Implement Template Markup
use_cases.description: Plan maintainable JSON-LD fields for repeated pages without stale hardcoded values.

use_cases.title: Reject Risky Markup
use_cases.description: Identify when FAQ, review, product, or event schema would misrepresent visible content.

prompt_templates.title: Check Eligibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether schema markup is appropriate for this page. Ask for missing details before recommending schema types.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Markup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page and its existing schema for alignment, required properties, warnings, and rich result eligibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Template Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a schema strategy for a templated content set. Include eligibility scoring, required fields, validation steps, and maintenance risks.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Entity Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare multiple schema types for this page and design a minimal @graph strategy that avoids conflicting entity definitions.

output_examples.input: Product page with visible price, availability, brand, and reviews.
output_examples.output: Eligibility score: 88, Strong Candidate. Recommended Product schema with visible offer data, review constraints, placement notes, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: FAQ section where questions are hidden behind marketing tabs.
output_examples.output: Eligibility score: 52, Do Not Implement. Main risks are hidden content, promotional intent, and likely rich result ineligibility.

output_examples.input: Blog article with author, date, headline, image, and breadcrumbs.
output_examples.output: Eligibility score: 82, Valid but Limited. Recommended Article and BreadcrumbList markup with monitoring in Search Console.

best_practices: Start with visible content and verify it supports each schema property.
Use the smallest set of schema types that supports the page goal.
Validate before release and monitor Search Console after deployment.
anti_patterns: Adding FAQ or review markup for content that users cannot see.
Hardcoding stale prices, availability, dates, or ratings into templates.
Creating schema only to target rich results without eligibility evidence.

faq.question: Can this skill guarantee rich results?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates eligibility and implementation quality, but Google decides whether rich results appear.

faq.question: Does it create JSON-LD guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design JSON-LD structure, placement instructions, and validation steps when schema is appropriate.

faq.question: Can it audit existing schema?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the page content and current markup so it can compare schema against visible content.

faq.question: Which schema types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common types including Organization, WebSite, Article, Product, FAQPage, HowTo, BreadcrumbList, LocalBusiness, Review, and Event.

faq.question: Does it run Google validation tools?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Rich Results Test, Schema.org Validator, and Search Console checks for the user to run.

faq.question: Is it useful for templated sites?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps plan dynamic fields and maintenance rules so template schema stays accurate.
